version.changelog:
wechat-article-fetch 1.0.0 – Initial Release

- Fetches WeChat Official Account article content (text only) from mp.weixin.qq.com links.
- Extracts and returns article title, main text, and actual URL after redirects.
- Uses Playwright to render and scrape content locally with Chromium.
- Designed for privacy: all processing is local, no data leaves your machine.
- Known limitations: cannot fetch content requiring login, paid articles, or from private accounts; images are not included, only their URLs.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: wechat-mp-fetch
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is a legitimate tool for scraping WeChat articles using Playwright. The code in `scripts/wx-article-fetch.js` correctly validates the target domain, uses headless browser automation to extract text content, and returns it as JSON without any evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and dependency list are consistent with its stated purpose (using Playwright to render a WeChat article and extract text); it does not request credentials or hidden access and contains no evidence of exfiltration or unrelated capabilities.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a Playwright-based Node script whose sole function is to load mp.weixin.qq.com article pages, extract title/content/url, and print JSON. The package.json dependency on Playwright is appropriate and there are no unrelated environment variables, binaries, or config paths requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the provided Node script which only visits the provided URL, waits for #js_content, extracts text, and prints JSON. One minor mismatch: SKILL.md claims "Playwright（运行脚本时会自动安装）" but the repository provides no installer hook; the environment must install dependencies (npm install) before running. Otherwise the runtime instructions stay within the stated purpose and do not access other files or credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no explicit install spec in the skill manifest (instruction-only), but package.json and package-lock.json declare playwright@^1.59.1. Playwright is a known public package (Playwright will also download browsers during install). The lockfile references registry.npmmirror.com (a public npm mirror) rather than a random URL — not ideal but not inherently malicious. Expect a large download (Chromium) when installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The code does not read environment secrets or other system files. This is proportionate for a web-scraping helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent agent-level privileges. It does not modify other skills or system settings. Runtime behavior creates transient browser instances and closes them.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do only what it says: run a headless Chromium via Playwright to render a WeChat article and extract text. Before running it: 1) be aware that installing and running will download Playwright and Chromium (large network downloads) and will cause the page you fetch to make its usual network requests (images/scripts) while rendering; that is normal but means remote hosts may receive requests from your machine. 2) SKILL.md's claim that Playwright will "auto-install when running the script" is environment-dependent — you should run npm install (or otherwise install dependencies) in a controlled environment first. 3) If you need stronger isolation, run the script in a sandbox/container or on an ephemeral VM to limit side-effects. 4) The package-lock references registry.npmmirror.com (a public npm mirror); if you prefer the official npm registry, run npm install using your preferred registry. 5) If you don't trust the author, review the script (it's short and readable) or run it in isolation; the code does not send extracted data to external endpoints or read credentials.
